   8class DatabaseManager:
   9    """
  10    Core database controller for the Cortex Pipeline.
  11    Manages connections to SQLite (local) or PostgreSQL (server) backends.
  12    """

  14    def __init__(self):
  15        """
  16        Handle   Init   operation.
  17        """
  18        from app.core import config
  19        
  20        # 1. First, connect based on the configuration
  21        if config.DB_TYPE == "postgres":
  22            try:
  23                import psycopg2
  24                self.conn = psycopg2.connect(**config.DB_CONFIG)
  25                self.cursor = self.conn.cursor() # <--- First define the cursor
  26                print(">> [Cortex] Connected to PostgreSQL Server.")
  27            except ImportError:
  28                print("!! [Error] psycopg2 not found.")
  29                return
  30        else:
  31            self.conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
  32            self.cursor = self.conn.cursor() # <--- First define the cursor
  33            print(f">> [Cortex] Using Local SQLite: {DB_PATH}")
  34        
  35        # 2. Now that the cursor is created, do the rest
  36        self.create_tables()
  37        self.perform_migrations()
  38        self.create_indexes() # <--- Now this line runs without error
  39        self.seed_data()

  41    def create_tables(self):

  49            )
  50        """)

 233    def create_indexes(self):
 234        """Building critical indexes to maintain speed in large projects"""
 235        try:
 236            # Index on entities (for fast loading of SHOT tasks)
 237            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_entity ON tasks(entity_id)")
 238            # Index on users (for fast loading of personal dashboard)
 239            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_assignee ON tasks(assignee_id)")
 240            # Index on dates (for quick reporting of future deadlines)
 241            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_due ON tasks(due_date)")
 242            
 243            self.conn.commit()
 244            print(">> [Cortex] Database Indexes verified.")
 245        except Exception as e:
 246            print(f"!! [Warning] Index creation failed: {e}")
 247
 248    def perform_migrations(self):
 249        """Check and intelligently repair the structure of the tables"""
 250        
 251        # --- 1. Checking the TASKS table ---
 252        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(tasks)")
 253        columns_info = self.cursor.fetchall()
 254        columns = [info[1] for info in columns_info]
 255        
 256        # A. Convert dept_id to department_id
 257        if "department_id" not in columns:
 258            print("Migration: Adding 'department_id' to tasks...")
 259            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN department_id TEXT")
 260        
 261        # If the old dept_id column exists, transfer its information
 262        if "dept_id" in columns:
 263            print("Migration: Transferring data from dept_id to department_id...")
 264            # This query only fills the places where department_id is empty
 265            self.cursor.execute("UPDATE tasks SET department_id = dept_id WHERE department_id IS NULL")
 266
 267        # B. Convert shot_id to entity_id
 268        if "entity_id" not in columns:
 269            print("Migration: Adding 'entity_id' to tasks...")
 270            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN entity_id TEXT")
 271        
 272        if "shot_id" in columns:
 273            print("Migration: Transferring data from shot_id to entity_id...")
 274            self.cursor.execute("UPDATE tasks SET entity_id = shot_id WHERE entity_id IS NULL")
 275
 276        # C. Add other new columns
 277        if "entity_type" not in columns:
 278            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN entity_type TEXT DEFAULT 'Shot'")
 279            
 280        if "assignee_id" not in columns:
 281            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN assignee_id TEXT")
 282            
 283        if "title" not in columns:
 284            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN title TEXT")
 285            
 286        if "description" not in columns:
 287            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN description TEXT")
 288
 289        # --- D. Add schedule columns (new migration) ---
 290        if "start_date" not in columns:
 291            print("Migration: Adding 'start_date' to tasks...")
 292            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN start_date TEXT")
 293            
 294        if "due_date" not in columns:
 295            print("Migration: Adding 'due_date' to tasks...")
 296            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT")
 297            
 298        if "estimated_hours" not in columns:
 299            print("Migration: Adding 'estimated_hours' to tasks...")
 300            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN estimated_hours REAL")
 301
 302        # --- 2. Checking the USERS table ---
 303        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(users)")
 304        user_cols = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 305        if "department_id" not in user_cols:
 306            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN department_id TEXT")
 307
 308        # --- Checking the PROJECTS table ---
 309        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(projects)")
 310        proj_columns = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 311        
 312        if "status" not in proj_columns:
 313            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN status TEXT DEFAULT 'Active'")
 314
 315        # --- Add new columns ---
 316        if "render_engine" not in proj_columns:
 317            print("Migration: Adding 'render_engine'...")
 318            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN render_engine TEXT DEFAULT '--------'")
 319            
 320        if "software" not in proj_columns:
 321            print("Migration: Adding 'software'...")
 322            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN software TEXT DEFAULT '--------'")
 323
 324        # --- Checking and updating the DEPARTMENTS table for locks ---
 325        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(departments)")
 326        dept_cols = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 327        
 328        if "allowed_software" not in dept_cols:
 329            print(">> [Migration] Adding 'allowed_software' to departments...")
 330            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE departments ADD COLUMN allowed_software TEXT DEFAULT 'all'")
 331            
 332        if "render_engine" not in dept_cols:
 333            print(">> [Migration] Adding 'render_engine' to departments...")
 334            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE departments ADD COLUMN render_engine TEXT DEFAULT '--------'")
 335
 336        # 1. Migration related to validation_rules (hold)
 337        try:
 338            self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(validation_rules)")
 339            val_columns = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 340            
 341            if "rule_script" not in val_columns:
 342                self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE validation_rules ADD COLUMN rule_script TEXT")
 343                self.conn.commit()
 344            
 345            if "is_mandatory" not in val_columns:
 346                self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE validation_rules ADD COLUMN is_mandatory INTEGER DEFAULT 1")
 347                self.conn.commit()
 348        except Exception as e:
 349            print(f"!! Migration Failed (Validation Rules): {e}")
 350
 351        # 2. Migration related to naming_standards (add)
 352        try:
 353            self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(naming_standards)")
 354            columns = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 355            if "project_id" not in columns:
 356                print(">> [Migration] Adding 'project_id' to naming_standards...")
 357                self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE naming_standards ADD COLUMN project_id TEXT")
 358                self.conn.commit()
 359        except Exception as e:
 360            print(f"!! Migration Error (Naming Standards): {e}")
 361
 362    def seed_data(self):
 363        """Create the primary user only if there is no user in the database"""
 364        self.cursor.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users")
 365        if self.cursor.fetchone()[0] == 0:
 366            # The database is empty, so create the primary user
 367            self.cursor.execute("INSERT INTO users VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
 368                                ("u1", "admin", "123456", "Admin", "admin", None))
 369
 370            self.cursor.execute("INSERT INTO projects VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
 371                                ("p1", "Project Titan", "TTN", r"D:\Projects\Titan", "Active", "Octane", "3ds Max"))
 372
 373            self.conn.commit()
 374            print("--- Database Initialized with Default User ---")

 378    def get_user_by_username(self, username):
 379        """
 380        Handle Get User By Username operation.
 381        """
 382        # There is no need to import models at the top of the file if we only return a tuple.
 383        # But because we create a model in Session, here we give raw data (Row) or model.
 384        # For simplicity, we import the model here
 385        from app.core.models import User
 386        
 387        self.cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=?", (username,))
 388        row = self.cursor.fetchone()
 389        if row:
 390            # row = (id, username, password, full_name, role, department_id)
 391            # We make sure the indexes are correct.
 392            # Because department_id is the last column (index 5).
 393            return User(id=row[0], username=row[1], full_name=row[3], role=row[4]) 
 394            # Note: We did not use password and department_id in simple User model
 395        return None

 412    def create_project(self, name, code, root_path, render_engine, software):
 413        """
 414        Handle Create Project operation.
 415        """
 416        new_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
 417        try:
 418            self.cursor.execute("INSERT INTO projects VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
 419                                (new_id, name, code, root_path, "Active", render_engine, software))
 420            self.conn.commit()
 421            return True
 422        except sqlite3.Error as e:

 426    def get_all_projects(self):
 427        """
 428        Handle Get All Projects operation.
 429        """
 430        from app.core.models import Project
 431        self.cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM projects")
 432        rows = self.cursor.fetchall()
 433        projects = []
 434        for row in rows:
 435            # Handling projects that may not have a status column (if the migration fails)
 436            # But since we have migration, we assume row[4] is status.
 437            status = row[4] if len(row) > 4 else "Active"
 438            render_engine = row[5] if len(row) > 5 else "--------"
 439            software = row[6] if len(row) > 6 else "--------"
 440            projects.append(Project(
 441                id=row[0], name=row[1], code=row[2], root_path=row[3],
 442                status=status, render_engine=render_engine, software=software
 443            ))
 444        return projects

 459    def delete_project(self, project_id):
 460        """Deleting the project and all its belongings (Shots, Assets, Tasks, Members)"""
 461        try:
 462            print(f">> Deleting project {project_id} and all children...")
 463            
 464            # 1. Removing tasks related to ASSETS
 465            self.cursor.execute("""
 466                DELETE FROM tasks WHERE entity_id IN (
 467                    SELECT id FROM assets WHERE project_id = ?
 468                )
 469            """, (project_id,))
 470
 471            # 2. Completely delete ASSETS
 472            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM assets WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 473
 474            # 3. Removing tasks related to SHOTS
 475            self.cursor.execute("""
 476                DELETE FROM tasks WHERE entity_id IN (
 477                    SELECT s.id FROM shots s
 478                    JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
 479                    WHERE seq.project_id = ?
 480                )
 481            """, (project_id,))
 482
 483            # 4. Delete all SHOTS
 484            self.cursor.execute("""
 485                DELETE FROM shots WHERE sequence_id IN (
 486                    SELECT id FROM sequences WHERE project_id = ?
 487                )
 488            """, (project_id,))
 489
 490            # 5. REMOVE ALL SEQUENCES
 491            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM sequences WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 492            
 493            # 6. Removal of project members
 494            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM project_members WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 495
 496            # 7. Delete the project itself
 497            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id=?", (project_id,))
 498            
 499            self.conn.commit()
 500            print(">> Project deleted successfully.")
 501            return True
 502            
 503        except sqlite3.Error as e:
 504            print(f"!! Project Delete Error: {e}")
 505            self.conn.rollback()
 506            return False

 508    def get_project_member_ids(self, project_id):
 509        """Returns the list of IDs of users who are members of the project"""
 510        self.cursor.execute("SELECT user_id FROM project_members WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 511        rows = self.cursor.fetchall()
 512        # Convert the list of tuples to a simple list of ids: ['id1', 'id2']
 513        return [row[0] for row in rows]

 515    def update_project_members(self, project_id, user_ids):
 516        """Replaces the list of project members with the new list"""
 517        try:
 518            # 1. First, delete all previous members of this project (Reset)
 519            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM project_members WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 520            
 521            # 2. Now add the new list (checkmarks).
 522            for user_id in user_ids:
 523                # We'll leave the permission_level at the default 'edit' for now
 524                self.cursor.execute("INSERT INTO project_members VALUES (?, ?, ?)", 
 525                                    (project_id, user_id, "edit"))
 526            
 527            self.conn.commit()
 528            return True
 529        except sqlite3.Error as e:
 530            print(f"Member Update Error: {e}")
 531            return False
 532        
 533    def get_project_users(self, project_id):
 534        """The complete list of users who are members of the project (to fill combobox)"""
 535        # This query pulls user information from the users table using JOIN
 536        # Provided that their ID is in the project_members table.
 537        query = """
 538            SELECT u.id, u.full_name, u.role 
 539            FROM users u
 540            JOIN project_members pm ON u.id = pm.user_id
 541            WHERE pm.project_id = ?
 542        """
 543        self.cursor.execute(query, (project_id,))
 544        return self.cursor.fetchall()

 580    def update_user(self, user_id, full_name, username, password, role, department_id):
 581        """Edit user information"""
 582        try:
 583            # Pay attention: the column name in the database is 'department_id', not 'dept_id'
 584            if password:
 585                query = """UPDATE users SET full_name=?, username=?, password=?, role=?, department_id=? WHERE id=?"""
 586                params = (full_name, username, password, role, department_id, user_id)

 989    def get_user_tasks(self, user_id, include_done=False):
 990        """
 991        Receive user tasks.
 992        include_done: If it is False, it will not show done tasks.
 993        """
 994        base_query = """
 995            SELECT 
 996                t.id, 
 997                t.status, 
 998                d.name, 
 999                COALESCE(p_shot.name, p_asset.name) as project_name,
1000                t.title, 
1001                t.description, 
1002                t.entity_id
1003            FROM tasks t
1004            LEFT JOIN departments d ON t.department_id = d.id
1005            
1006            LEFT JOIN shots s ON t.entity_id = s.id
1007            LEFT JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
1008            LEFT JOIN projects p_shot ON seq.project_id = p_shot.id
1009            
1010            LEFT JOIN assets a ON t.entity_id = a.id
1011            LEFT JOIN projects p_asset ON a.project_id = p_asset.id
1012            
1013            WHERE t.assignee_id = ?
1014            AND (p_shot.id IS NOT NULL OR p_asset.id IS NOT NULL)
1015        """
1016        
1017        # If the Show completed tasks tick is off, filter
1018        if not include_done:
1019            base_query += " AND t.status != 'Done'"
1020            
1021        # Sort: Newer works up
1022        base_query += " ORDER BY t.status DESC"
1023
1024        self.cursor.execute(base_query, (user_id,))
1025        return self.cursor.fetchall()
1026        
1027    def get_task_context_data(self, task_id):
1028        """
1029        Retrieves full contextual information for a specific task to be used by launchers.
1030        
1031        Args:
1032            task_id (str): Unique UUID of the task.
1033            
1034        Returns:
1035            dict: Comprehensive data including project path, entity name, and frame ranges.
1036            None: If the task ID is not found.
1037        """
1038        # First we take the task itself
1039        task = self.get_task_by_id(task_id)
1040        if not task: return None
1041        
1042        # task = (id, status, dept_name, user_name, color, title, desc, entity_id, dept_id, assignee_id)
1043        entity_id = task[7]
1044        task_title = task[5]
1045
1046        # 1. Let's check if it is SHOT?
1047        self.cursor.execute("""
1048            SELECT s.id, s.name, s.frame_start, s.frame_end, seq.name, p.id, p.name, p.root_path
1049            FROM shots s
1050            JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
1051            JOIN projects p ON seq.project_id = p.id
1052            WHERE s.id = ?
1053        """, (entity_id,))
1054        shot_data = self.cursor.fetchone()
1055        
1056        if shot_data:
1057            return {
1058                "type": "Shot",
1059                "entity_id": shot_data[0],        # <--- This line must be
1060                "task_id": task_id,
1061                "task_title": task_title,
1062                "entity_name": shot_data[1],      
1063                "parent_name": shot_data[4],      
1064                "frame_start": shot_data[2],
1065                "frame_end": shot_data[3],
1066                "project_id": shot_data[5],
1067                "project_name": shot_data[6],
1068                "project_root": shot_data[7]
1069            }
1070
1071        # 2. Let's check if it is an ASSET?
1072        self.cursor.execute("""
1073            SELECT a.id, a.name, a.category, p.id, p.name, p.root_path
1074            FROM assets a
1075            JOIN projects p ON a.project_id = p.id
1076            WHERE a.id = ?
1077        """, (entity_id,))
1078        asset_data = self.cursor.fetchone()
1079
1080        if asset_data:
1081            return {
1082                "type": "Asset",
1083                "entity_id": asset_data[0],       # <--- This line was left!
1084                "task_id": task_id,
1085                "task_title": task_title,
1086                "entity_name": asset_data[1],     # Asset Name (Batman)
1087                "parent_name": asset_data[2],     # Category (Characters)
1088                "frame_start": 1001,              # Default for Asset
1089                "frame_end": 1001,                # Default for Asset
1090                "project_id": asset_data[3],
1091                "project_name": asset_data[4],
1092                "project_root": asset_data[5]
1093            }
1094            
1095        return None
1096

1189    def create_publish(self, task_id, version, comment, user_name, thumbnail_path, files_dict):
1190        """
1191        Registers a new publish entry and links its associated files.
1192        
1193        Args:
1194            task_id (str): The task being published.
1195            version (int): Incremental version number.
1196            comment (str): Artist's description of changes.
1197            user_name (str): Name of the publisher.
1198            thumbnail_path (str): Path to the generated preview image.
1199            files_dict (dict): Dictionary mapping file types to their physical paths.
1200            
1201        Returns:
1202            tuple: (bool success, str publish_id or error_message).
1203        """
1204        import uuid
1205        pub_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
1206        
1207        try:
1208            # 1. Registration of self-publishing
1209            self.cursor.execute("""
1210                INSERT INTO publishes (id, task_id, version, comment, created_by, thumbnail_path)
1211                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
1212            """, (pub_id, task_id, version, comment, user_name, thumbnail_path))
1213            
1214            # 2. Registration of individual files
1215            for f_type, f_path in files_dict.items():
1216                file_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
1217                self.cursor.execute("""
1218                    INSERT INTO published_files (id, publish_id, file_type, file_path)
1219                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
1220                """, (file_id, pub_id, f_type, f_path))
1221            
1222            self.conn.commit()
1223            return True, pub_id
1224            
1225        except sqlite3.Error as e:
1226            print(f"Publish DB Error: {e}")
1227            return False, str(e)

1235    def get_publish_path(self, task_id, software="max", category="3d"):
1236        """
1237        Generation of intelligent publishing path based on the structure defined in the file system
1238        """
1239        context = self.get_task_context_data(task_id)
1240        if not context:
1241            return None
1242            
1243        root = context['project_root']
1244        proj = context['project_name']
1245        entity_dir = "Assets" if context['type'] == 'Asset' else "Sequences"
1246        
1247        # Asset or shot root path: D:/.../Project Titan/Assets/Characters/Hero
1248        base_path = os.path.join(root, proj, entity_dir, context['parent_name'], context['entity_name'])
1249        
1250        # Read structure from configuration (or use default)
1251        from app.core.filesystem import FileSystemManager
1252        if context['type'] == 'Asset':
1253            structure = FileSystemManager.get_asset_structure(self)
1254        else:
1255            structure = FileSystemManager.get_shot_structure(self)
1256            
1257        # Checking if category (eg 3d or 2d) is defined in the publish folder?
1258        # Default assumption: publish -> 3d -> max
1259        publish_dir = "publish"
1260        
1261        # Make the final path: base_path / publish / category / software
1262        # Example: D:/.../Hero/publish/3d/max
1263        final_path = os.path.join(base_path, publish_dir, category, software).replace("\\", "/")
1264        
1265        return final_path

  10    """
  11    Core database controller for the Cortex Pipeline.

  15    def __init__(self):
  16        """
  17        Handle   Init   operation.
  18        """
  19        from app.core import config
  20        
  21        # 1. First, connect based on the configuration
  22        if config.DB_TYPE == "postgres":
  23            try:
  24                import psycopg2
  25                self.conn = psycopg2.connect(**config.DB_CONFIG)
  26                self.cursor = self.conn.cursor() # <--- First define the cursor
  27                print(">> [Cortex] Connected to PostgreSQL Server.")
  28            except ImportError:

  30                return
  31        else:
  32            self.conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)

  34            print(f">> [Cortex] Using Local SQLite: {DB_PATH}")
  35        
  36        # 2. Now that the cursor is created, do the rest
  37        self.create_tables()
  38        self.perform_migrations()
  39        self.create_indexes() # <--- Now this line runs without error
  40        self.seed_data()

  42    def create_tables(self):

  65
  66        # Projects

  68            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS projects (
  69                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

 100        # Shots

 142        # Assets

 144            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS assets (
 145                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

 151            )

 162        # Publishes

 164            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS publishes (
 165                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

 234    def create_indexes(self):
 235        """Building critical indexes to maintain speed in large projects"""
 236        try:
 237            # Index on entities (for fast loading of SHOT tasks)
 238            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_entity ON tasks(entity_id)")
 239            # Index on users (for fast loading of personal dashboard)
 240            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_assignee ON tasks(assignee_id)")
 241            # Index on dates (for quick reporting of future deadlines)
 242            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_due ON tasks(due_date)")
 243            
 244            self.conn.commit()
 245            print(">> [Cortex] Database Indexes verified.")
 246        except Exception as e:
 247            print(f"!! [Warning] Index creation failed: {e}")
 248
 249    def perform_migrations(self):
 250        """Check and intelligently repair the structure of the tables"""
 251        
 252        # --- 1. Checking the TASKS table ---
 253        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(tasks)")
 254        columns_info = self.cursor.fetchall()
 255        columns = [info[1] for info in columns_info]
 256        
 257        # A. Convert dept_id to department_id
 258        if "department_id" not in columns:
 259            print("Migration: Adding 'department_id' to tasks...")
 260            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN department_id TEXT")
 261        
 262        # If the old dept_id column exists, transfer its information
 263        if "dept_id" in columns:
 264            print("Migration: Transferring data from dept_id to department_id...")
 265            # This query only fills the places where department_id is empty
 266            self.cursor.execute("UPDATE tasks SET department_id = dept_id WHERE department_id IS NULL")
 267
 268        # B. Convert shot_id to entity_id
 269        if "entity_id" not in columns:
 270            print("Migration: Adding 'entity_id' to tasks...")
 271            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN entity_id TEXT")
 272        
 273        if "shot_id" in columns:
 274            print("Migration: Transferring data from shot_id to entity_id...")
 275            self.cursor.execute("UPDATE tasks SET entity_id = shot_id WHERE entity_id IS NULL")
 276
 277        # C. Add other new columns
 278        if "entity_type" not in columns:
 279            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN entity_type TEXT DEFAULT 'Shot'")
 280            
 281        if "assignee_id" not in columns:
 282            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN assignee_id TEXT")
 283            
 284        if "title" not in columns:
 285            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN title TEXT")
 286            
 287        if "description" not in columns:
 288            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN description TEXT")
 289
 290        # --- D. Add schedule columns (new migration) ---
 291        if "start_date" not in columns:
 292            print("Migration: Adding 'start_date' to tasks...")
 293            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN start_date TEXT")
 294            
 295        if "due_date" not in columns:
 296            print("Migration: Adding 'due_date' to tasks...")
 297            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT")
 298            
 299        if "estimated_hours" not in columns:
 300            print("Migration: Adding 'estimated_hours' to tasks...")
 301            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN estimated_hours REAL")
 302
 303        # --- 2. Checking the USERS table ---
 304        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(users)")
 305        user_cols = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 306        if "department_id" not in user_cols:
 307            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN department_id TEXT")
 308
 309        # --- Checking the PROJECTS table ---
 310        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(projects)")
 311        proj_columns = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 312        
 313        if "status" not in proj_columns:
 314            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN status TEXT DEFAULT 'Active'")
 315
 316        # --- Add new columns ---
 317        if "render_engine" not in proj_columns:
 318            print("Migration: Adding 'render_engine'...")
 319            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN render_engine TEXT DEFAULT '--------'")
 320            
 321        if "software" not in proj_columns:
 322            print("Migration: Adding 'software'...")
 323            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE projects ADD COLUMN software TEXT DEFAULT '--------'")
 324
 325        # --- Checking and updating the DEPARTMENTS table for locks ---
 326        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(departments)")
 327        dept_cols = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 328        
 329        if "allowed_software" not in dept_cols:
 330            print(">> [Migration] Adding 'allowed_software' to departments...")
 331            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE departments ADD COLUMN allowed_software TEXT DEFAULT 'all'")
 332            
 333        if "render_engine" not in dept_cols:
 334            print(">> [Migration] Adding 'render_engine' to departments...")
 335            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE departments ADD COLUMN render_engine TEXT DEFAULT '--------'")
 336
 337        # 1. Migration related to validation_rules (hold)
 338        try:
 339            self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(validation_rules)")
 340            val_columns = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 341            
 342            if "rule_script" not in val_columns:
 343                self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE validation_rules ADD COLUMN rule_script TEXT")
 344                self.conn.commit()
 345            
 346            if "is_mandatory" not in val_columns:
 347                self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE validation_rules ADD COLUMN is_mandatory INTEGER DEFAULT 1")
 348                self.conn.commit()
 349        except Exception as e:
 350            print(f"!! Migration Failed (Validation Rules): {e}")
 351
 352        # 2. Migration related to naming_standards (add)
 353        try:
 354            self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(naming_standards)")
 355            columns = [info[1] for info in self.cursor.fetchall()]
 356            if "project_id" not in columns:
 357                print(">> [Migration] Adding 'project_id' to naming_standards...")
 358                self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE naming_standards ADD COLUMN project_id TEXT")
 359                self.conn.commit()
 360        except Exception as e:
 361            print(f"!! Migration Error (Naming Standards): {e}")
 362
 363    def seed_data(self):
 364        """Create the primary user only if there is no user in the database"""

 366        if self.cursor.fetchone()[0] == 0:
 367            # The database is empty, so create the primary user
 368            self.cursor.execute("INSERT INTO users VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
 369                                ("u1", "admin", "123456", "Admin", "admin", None))
 370
 371            self.cursor.execute("INSERT INTO projects VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
 372                                ("p1", "Project Titan", "TTN", r"D:\Projects\Titan", "Active", "Octane", "3ds Max"))
 373
 374            self.conn.commit()
 375            print("--- Database Initialized with Default User ---")

 379    def get_user_by_username(self, username):
 380        """
 381        Handle Get User By Username operation.
 382        """
 383        # There is no need to import models at the top of the file if we only return a tuple.
 384        # But because we create a model in Session, here we give raw data (Row) or model.
 385        # For simplicity, we import the model here
 386        from app.core.models import User
 387        
 388        self.cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=?", (username,))
 389        row = self.cursor.fetchone()
 390        if row:
 391            # row = (id, username, password, full_name, role, department_id)
 392            # We make sure the indexes are correct.
 393            # Because department_id is the last column (index 5).
 394            return User(id=row[0], username=row[1], full_name=row[3], role=row[4]) 
 395            # Note: We did not use password and department_id in simple User model
 396        return None

 427    def get_all_projects(self):
 428        """
 429        Handle Get All Projects operation.
 430        """
 431        from app.core.models import Project
 432        self.cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM projects")
 433        rows = self.cursor.fetchall()
 434        projects = []
 435        for row in rows:
 436            # Handling projects that may not have a status column (if the migration fails)
 437            # But since we have migration, we assume row[4] is status.
 438            status = row[4] if len(row) > 4 else "Active"
 439            render_engine = row[5] if len(row) > 5 else "--------"
 440            software = row[6] if len(row) > 6 else "--------"
 441            projects.append(Project(
 442                id=row[0], name=row[1], code=row[2], root_path=row[3],
 443                status=status, render_engine=render_engine, software=software
 444            ))
 445        return projects

 453            self.cursor.execute(query, (name, code, root_path, status, render_engine, software, project_id))

 460    def delete_project(self, project_id):
 461        """Deleting the project and all its belongings (Shots, Assets, Tasks, Members)"""
 462        try:
 463            print(f">> Deleting project {project_id} and all children...")
 464            
 465            # 1. Removing tasks related to ASSETS
 466            self.cursor.execute("""
 467                DELETE FROM tasks WHERE entity_id IN (
 468                    SELECT id FROM assets WHERE project_id = ?
 469                )
 470            """, (project_id,))
 471
 472            # 2. Completely delete ASSETS
 473            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM assets WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 474
 475            # 3. Removing tasks related to SHOTS
 476            self.cursor.execute("""
 477                DELETE FROM tasks WHERE entity_id IN (
 478                    SELECT s.id FROM shots s
 479                    JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
 480                    WHERE seq.project_id = ?
 481                )
 482            """, (project_id,))
 483
 484            # 4. Delete all SHOTS
 485            self.cursor.execute("""
 486                DELETE FROM shots WHERE sequence_id IN (
 487                    SELECT id FROM sequences WHERE project_id = ?
 488                )
 489            """, (project_id,))
 490
 491            # 5. REMOVE ALL SEQUENCES
 492            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM sequences WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 493            
 494            # 6. Removal of project members
 495            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM project_members WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 496
 497            # 7. Delete the project itself
 498            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id=?", (project_id,))
 499            
 500            self.conn.commit()
 501            print(">> Project deleted successfully.")
 502            return True
 503            
 504        except sqlite3.Error as e:
 505            print(f"!! Project Delete Error: {e}")
 506            self.conn.rollback()
 507            return False
 508        
 509    def get_project_member_ids(self, project_id):
 510        """Returns the list of IDs of users who are members of the project"""
 511        self.cursor.execute("SELECT user_id FROM project_members WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 512        rows = self.cursor.fetchall()
 513        # Convert the list of tuples to a simple list of ids: ['id1', 'id2']
 514        return [row[0] for row in rows]

 516    def update_project_members(self, project_id, user_ids):
 517        """Replaces the list of project members with the new list"""
 518        try:
 519            # 1. First, delete all previous members of this project (Reset)
 520            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM project_members WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
 521            
 522            # 2. Now add the new list (checkmarks).
 523            for user_id in user_ids:
 524                # We'll leave the permission_level at the default 'edit' for now
 525                self.cursor.execute("INSERT INTO project_members VALUES (?, ?, ?)", 
 526                                    (project_id, user_id, "edit"))
 527            
 528            self.conn.commit()
 529            return True
 530        except sqlite3.Error as e:
 531            print(f"Member Update Error: {e}")
 532            return False

 534    def get_project_users(self, project_id):
 535        """The complete list of users who are members of the project (to fill combobox)"""
 536        # This query pulls user information from the users table using JOIN
 537        # Provided that their ID is in the project_members table.
 538        query = """
 539            SELECT u.id, u.full_name, u.role 
 540            FROM users u
 541            JOIN project_members pm ON u.id = pm.user_id
 542            WHERE pm.project_id = ?
 543        """
 544        self.cursor.execute(query, (project_id,))
 545        return self.cursor.fetchall()

 990    def get_user_tasks(self, user_id, include_done=False):
 991        """
 992        Receive user tasks.
 993        include_done: If it is False, it will not show done tasks.
 994        """
 995        base_query = """
 996            SELECT 
 997                t.id, 
 998                t.status, 
 999                d.name, 
1000                COALESCE(p_shot.name, p_asset.name) as project_name,
1001                t.title, 
1002                t.description, 
1003                t.entity_id
1004            FROM tasks t
1005            LEFT JOIN departments d ON t.department_id = d.id
1006            
1007            LEFT JOIN shots s ON t.entity_id = s.id
1008            LEFT JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
1009            LEFT JOIN projects p_shot ON seq.project_id = p_shot.id
1010            
1011            LEFT JOIN assets a ON t.entity_id = a.id
1012            LEFT JOIN projects p_asset ON a.project_id = p_asset.id
1013            
1014            WHERE t.assignee_id = ?
1015            AND (p_shot.id IS NOT NULL OR p_asset.id IS NOT NULL)
1016        """
1017        
1018        # If the Show completed tasks tick is off, filter
1019        if not include_done:
1020            base_query += " AND t.status != 'Done'"
1021            
1022        # Sort: Newer works up
1023        base_query += " ORDER BY t.status DESC"
1024
1025        self.cursor.execute(base_query, (user_id,))
1026        return self.cursor.fetchall()
1027        
1028    def get_task_context_data(self, task_id):
1029        """
1030        Retrieves full contextual information for a specific task to be used by launchers.
1031        
1032        Args:
1033            task_id (str): Unique UUID of the task.
1034            
1035        Returns:
1036            dict: Comprehensive data including project path, entity name, and frame ranges.
1037            None: If the task ID is not found.
1038        """
1039        # First we take the task itself
1040        task = self.get_task_by_id(task_id)
1041        if not task: return None
1042        
1043        # task = (id, status, dept_name, user_name, color, title, desc, entity_id, dept_id, assignee_id)
1044        entity_id = task[7]
1045        task_title = task[5]
1046
1047        # 1. Let's check if it is SHOT?
1048        self.cursor.execute("""
1049            SELECT s.id, s.name, s.frame_start, s.frame_end, seq.name, p.id, p.name, p.root_path
1050            FROM shots s
1051            JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
1052            JOIN projects p ON seq.project_id = p.id
1053            WHERE s.id = ?
1054        """, (entity_id,))
1055        shot_data = self.cursor.fetchone()
1056        
1057        if shot_data:
1058            return {
1059                "type": "Shot",
1060                "entity_id": shot_data[0],        # <--- This line must be
1061                "task_id": task_id,
1062                "task_title": task_title,
1063                "entity_name": shot_data[1],      
1064                "parent_name": shot_data[4],      
1065                "frame_start": shot_data[2],
1066                "frame_end": shot_data[3],
1067                "project_id": shot_data[5],
1068                "project_name": shot_data[6],
1069                "project_root": shot_data[7]
1070            }
1071
1072        # 2. Let's check if it is an ASSET?
1073        self.cursor.execute("""
1074            SELECT a.id, a.name, a.category, p.id, p.name, p.root_path
1075            FROM assets a
1076            JOIN projects p ON a.project_id = p.id
1077            WHERE a.id = ?
1078        """, (entity_id,))
1079        asset_data = self.cursor.fetchone()
1080
1081        if asset_data:
1082            return {
1083                "type": "Asset",
1084                "entity_id": asset_data[0],       # <--- This line was left!
1085                "task_id": task_id,
1086                "task_title": task_title,
1087                "entity_name": asset_data[1],     # Asset Name (Batman)
1088                "parent_name": asset_data[2],     # Category (Characters)
1089                "frame_start": 1001,              # Default for Asset
1090                "frame_end": 1001,                # Default for Asset
1091                "project_id": asset_data[3],
1092                "project_name": asset_data[4],
1093                "project_root": asset_data[5]
1094            }
1095            
1096        return None
1097

1190    def create_publish(self, task_id, version, comment, user_name, thumbnail_path, files_dict):
1191        """
1192        Registers a new publish entry and links its associated files.
1193        
1194        Args:
1195            task_id (str): The task being published.
1196            version (int): Incremental version number.
1197            comment (str): Artist's description of changes.
1198            user_name (str): Name of the publisher.
1199            thumbnail_path (str): Path to the generated preview image.
1200            files_dict (dict): Dictionary mapping file types to their physical paths.
1201            
1202        Returns:
1203            tuple: (bool success, str publish_id or error_message).
1204        """
1205        import uuid
1206        pub_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
1207        
1208        try:
1209            # 1. Registration of self-publishing
1210            self.cursor.execute("""
1211                INSERT INTO publishes (id, task_id, version, comment, created_by, thumbnail_path)
1212                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
1213            """, (pub_id, task_id, version, comment, user_name, thumbnail_path))
1214            
1215            # 2. Registration of individual files
1216            for f_type, f_path in files_dict.items():
1217                file_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
1218                self.cursor.execute("""
1219                    INSERT INTO published_files (id, publish_id, file_type, file_path)
1220                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
1221                """, (file_id, pub_id, f_type, f_path))
1222            
1223            self.conn.commit()
1224            return True, pub_id
1225            
1226        except sqlite3.Error as e:
1227            print(f"Publish DB Error: {e}")
1228            return False, str(e)
1229

1232        self.cursor.execute("SELECT MAX(version) FROM publishes WHERE task_id=?", (task_id,))
1233        row = self.cursor.fetchone()
1234        return row[0] if row[0] else 0

1236    def get_publish_path(self, task_id, software="max", category="3d"):
1237        """
1238        Generation of intelligent publishing path based on the structure defined in the file system
1239        """
1240        context = self.get_task_context_data(task_id)
1241        if not context:
1242            return None
1243            
1244        root = context['project_root']
1245        proj = context['project_name']
1246        entity_dir = "Assets" if context['type'] == 'Asset' else "Sequences"
1247        
1248        # Asset or shot root path: D:/.../Project Titan/Assets/Characters/Hero
1249        base_path = os.path.join(root, proj, entity_dir, context['parent_name'], context['entity_name'])
1250        
1251        # Read structure from configuration (or use default)
1252        from app.core.filesystem import FileSystemManager
1253        if context['type'] == 'Asset':
1254            structure = FileSystemManager.get_asset_structure(self)
1255        else:
1256            structure = FileSystemManager.get_shot_structure(self)
1257            
1258        # Checking if category (eg 3d or 2d) is defined in the publish folder?
1259        # Default assumption: publish -> 3d -> max
1260        publish_dir = "publish"
1261        
1262        # Make the final path: base_path / publish / category / software
1263        # Example: D:/.../Hero/publish/3d/max
1264        final_path = os.path.join(base_path, publish_dir, category, software).replace("\\", "/")
1265        
1266        return final_path

 42    def create_tables(self):

def create_indexes(self): 
234    def create_indexes(self):
235        """Building critical indexes to maintain speed in large projects"""
236        try:
237            # Index on entities (for fast loading of SHOT tasks)
238            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_entity ON tasks(entity_id)")
239            # Index on users (for fast loading of personal dashboard)
240            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_assignee ON tasks(assignee_id)")
241            # Index on dates (for quick reporting of future deadlines)
242            self.cursor.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tasks_due ON tasks(due_date)")
243            
244            self.conn.commit()
245            print(">> [Cortex] Database Indexes verified.")
246        except Exception as e:
247            print(f"!! [Warning] Index creation failed: {e}")

Building critical indexes to maintain speed in large projects

def perform_migrations(self): 
249    def perform_migrations(self):
250        """Check and intelligently repair the structure of the tables"""
251        
252        # --- 1. Checking the TASKS table ---
253        self.cursor.execute("PRAGMA table_info(tasks)")
254        columns_info = self.cursor.fetchall()
255        columns = [info[1] for info in columns_info]
256        
257        # A. Convert dept_id to department_id
258        if "department_id" not in columns:
259            print("Migration: Adding 'department_id' to tasks...")
260            self.cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN department_id TEXT")

def delete_project(self, project_id): 
460    def delete_project(self, project_id):
461        """Deleting the project and all its belongings (Shots, Assets, Tasks, Members)"""
462        try:
463            print(f">> Deleting project {project_id} and all children...")
464            
465            # 1. Removing tasks related to ASSETS
466            self.cursor.execute("""
467                DELETE FROM tasks WHERE entity_id IN (
468                    SELECT id FROM assets WHERE project_id = ?
469                )
470            """, (project_id,))
471
472            # 2. Completely delete ASSETS
473            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM assets WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
474
475            # 3. Removing tasks related to SHOTS
476            self.cursor.execute("""
477                DELETE FROM tasks WHERE entity_id IN (
478                    SELECT s.id FROM shots s
479                    JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
480                    WHERE seq.project_id = ?
481                )
482            """, (project_id,))
483
484            # 4. Delete all SHOTS
485            self.cursor.execute("""
486                DELETE FROM shots WHERE sequence_id IN (
487                    SELECT id FROM sequences WHERE project_id = ?
488                )
489            """, (project_id,))
490
491            # 5. REMOVE ALL SEQUENCES
492            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM sequences WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
493            
494            # 6. Removal of project members
495            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM project_members WHERE project_id=?", (project_id,))
496
497            # 7. Delete the project itself
498            self.cursor.execute("DELETE FROM projects WHERE id=?", (project_id,))
499            
500            self.conn.commit()
501            print(">> Project deleted successfully.")
502            return True
503            
504        except sqlite3.Error as e:
505            print(f"!! Project Delete Error: {e}")
506            self.conn.rollback()
507            return False

Deleting the project and all its belongings (Shots, Assets, Tasks, Members)

def get_user_tasks(self, user_id, include_done=False): 
 990    def get_user_tasks(self, user_id, include_done=False):
 991        """
 992        Receive user tasks.
 993        include_done: If it is False, it will not show done tasks.
 994        """
 995        base_query = """
 996            SELECT 
 997                t.id, 
 998                t.status, 
 999                d.name, 
1000                COALESCE(p_shot.name, p_asset.name) as project_name,
1001                t.title, 
1002                t.description, 
1003                t.entity_id
1004            FROM tasks t
1005            LEFT JOIN departments d ON t.department_id = d.id
1006            
1007            LEFT JOIN shots s ON t.entity_id = s.id
1008            LEFT JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
1009            LEFT JOIN projects p_shot ON seq.project_id = p_shot.id
1010            
1011            LEFT JOIN assets a ON t.entity_id = a.id
1012            LEFT JOIN projects p_asset ON a.project_id = p_asset.id
1013            
1014            WHERE t.assignee_id = ?
1015            AND (p_shot.id IS NOT NULL OR p_asset.id IS NOT NULL)
1016        """
1017        
1018        # If the Show completed tasks tick is off, filter
1019        if not include_done:
1020            base_query += " AND t.status != 'Done'"
1021            
1022        # Sort: Newer works up
1023        base_query += " ORDER BY t.status DESC"
1024
1025        self.cursor.execute(base_query, (user_id,))
1026        return self.cursor.fetchall()

Receive user tasks. include_done: If it is False, it will not show done tasks.

def get_task_context_data(self, task_id): 
1028    def get_task_context_data(self, task_id):
1029        """
1030        Retrieves full contextual information for a specific task to be used by launchers.
1031        
1032        Args:
1033            task_id (str): Unique UUID of the task.
1034            
1035        Returns:
1036            dict: Comprehensive data including project path, entity name, and frame ranges.
1037            None: If the task ID is not found.
1038        """
1039        # First we take the task itself
1040        task = self.get_task_by_id(task_id)
1041        if not task: return None
1042        
1043        # task = (id, status, dept_name, user_name, color, title, desc, entity_id, dept_id, assignee_id)
1044        entity_id = task[7]
1045        task_title = task[5]
1046
1047        # 1. Let's check if it is SHOT?
1048        self.cursor.execute("""
1049            SELECT s.id, s.name, s.frame_start, s.frame_end, seq.name, p.id, p.name, p.root_path
1050            FROM shots s
1051            JOIN sequences seq ON s.sequence_id = seq.id
1052            JOIN projects p ON seq.project_id = p.id
1053            WHERE s.id = ?
1054        """, (entity_id,))
1055        shot_data = self.cursor.fetchone()
1056        
1057        if shot_data:
1058            return {
1059                "type": "Shot",
1060                "entity_id": shot_data[0],        # <--- This line must be
1061                "task_id": task_id,
1062                "task_title": task_title,
1063                "entity_name": shot_data[1],      
1064                "parent_name": shot_data[4],      
1065                "frame_start": shot_data[2],
1066                "frame_end": shot_data[3],
1067                "project_id": shot_data[5],
1068                "project_name": shot_data[6],
1069                "project_root": shot_data[7]
1070            }
1071
1072        # 2. Let's check if it is an ASSET?
1073        self.cursor.execute("""
1074            SELECT a.id, a.name, a.category, p.id, p.name, p.root_path
1075            FROM assets a
1076            JOIN projects p ON a.project_id = p.id
1077            WHERE a.id = ?
1078        """, (entity_id,))
1079        asset_data = self.cursor.fetchone()
1080
1081        if asset_data:
1082            return {
1083                "type": "Asset",
1084                "entity_id": asset_data[0],       # <--- This line was left!
1085                "task_id": task_id,
1086                "task_title": task_title,
1087                "entity_name": asset_data[1],     # Asset Name (Batman)
1088                "parent_name": asset_data[2],     # Category (Characters)
1089                "frame_start": 1001,              # Default for Asset
1090                "frame_end": 1001,                # Default for Asset
1091                "project_id": asset_data[3],
1092                "project_name": asset_data[4],
1093                "project_root": asset_data[5]
1094            }
1095            
1096        return None

Retrieves full contextual information for a specific task to be used by launchers.

Args: task_id (str): Unique UUID of the task.

Returns: dict: Comprehensive data including project path, entity name, and frame ranges. None: If the task ID is not found.

def create_publish( self, task_id, version, comment, user_name, thumbnail_path, files_dict): 
1190    def create_publish(self, task_id, version, comment, user_name, thumbnail_path, files_dict):
1191        """
1192        Registers a new publish entry and links its associated files.
1193        
1194        Args:
1195            task_id (str): The task being published.
1196            version (int): Incremental version number.
1197            comment (str): Artist's description of changes.
1198            user_name (str): Name of the publisher.
1199            thumbnail_path (str): Path to the generated preview image.
1200            files_dict (dict): Dictionary mapping file types to their physical paths.
1201            
1202        Returns:
1203            tuple: (bool success, str publish_id or error_message).
1204        """
1205        import uuid
1206        pub_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
1207        
1208        try:
1209            # 1. Registration of self-publishing
1210            self.cursor.execute("""
1211                INSERT INTO publishes (id, task_id, version, comment, created_by, thumbnail_path)
1212                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
1213            """, (pub_id, task_id, version, comment, user_name, thumbnail_path))
1214            
1215            # 2. Registration of individual files
1216            for f_type, f_path in files_dict.items():
1217                file_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
1218                self.cursor.execute("""
1219                    INSERT INTO published_files (id, publish_id, file_type, file_path)
1220                    VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
1221                """, (file_id, pub_id, f_type, f_path))
1222            
1223            self.conn.commit()
1224            return True, pub_id
1225            
1226        except sqlite3.Error as e:
1227            print(f"Publish DB Error: {e}")
1228            return False, str(e)

Registers a new publish entry and links its associated files.

def get_publish_path(self, task_id, software='max', category='3d'): 
1236    def get_publish_path(self, task_id, software="max", category="3d"):
1237        """
1238        Generation of intelligent publishing path based on the structure defined in the file system
1239        """
1240        context = self.get_task_context_data(task_id)
1241        if not context:
1242            return None
1243            
1244        root = context['project_root']
1245        proj = context['project_name']
1246        entity_dir = "Assets" if context['type'] == 'Asset' else "Sequences"
1247        
1248        # Asset or shot root path: D:/.../Project Titan/Assets/Characters/Hero
1249        base_path = os.path.join(root, proj, entity_dir, context['parent_name'], context['entity_name'])
1250        
1251        # Read structure from configuration (or use default)
1252        from app.core.filesystem import FileSystemManager
1253        if context['type'] == 'Asset':
1254            structure = FileSystemManager.get_asset_structure(self)
1255        else:
1256            structure = FileSystemManager.get_shot_structure(self)
1257            
1258        # Checking if category (eg 3d or 2d) is defined in the publish folder?
1259        # Default assumption: publish -> 3d -> max
1260        publish_dir = "publish"
1261        
1262        # Make the final path: base_path / publish / category / software
1263        # Example: D:/.../Hero/publish/3d/max
1264        final_path = os.path.join(base_path, publish_dir, category, software).replace("\\", "/")
1265        
1266        return final_path

Generation of intelligent publishing path based on the structure defined in the file system
